questions.prompt: Which statement best matches the syllabus focus of “Input Validation and Fail-Fast Design”?
options: This means disabling static analysis and treating every runtime value as a trusted type.
This is a deployment-only detail that can be ignored while writing and testing source code.
Preconditions, postconditions, and validating untrusted values
This is exclusively a Flutter widget/rendering concern and has no relationship to Dart language or tooling.
questions.answer_key: Preconditions, postconditions, and validating untrusted values
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus describes this lesson as: Preconditions, postconditions, and validating untrusted values.

questions.prompt: Which first step is most useful when applying “Input Validation and Fail-Fast Design” in a small Dart program?
options: Assume that a successful native run proves the same APIs and behavior are available on web targets.
Build a minimal Dart example for Input Validation and Fail-Fast Design, predict its behavior, and verify an edge case before integrating it.
Change multiple unrelated parts until the output appears plausible, then skip a repeatable test.
Copy a dependency version without checking its SDK constraint, maintenance, license, or API documentation.
questions.answer_key: Build a minimal Dart example for Input Validation and Fail-Fast Design, predict its behavior, and verify an edge case before integrating it.
questions.explanation: A minimal example and an explicit boundary check make the behavior easier to verify and maintain.

questions.prompt: If a program involving “Input Validation and Fail-Fast Design” behaves unexpectedly, which response is most reliable?
options: Reduce the failure to a small case, inspect the complete diagnostic and inputs, verify the documented SDK/target constraints, and test one change at a time.
Suppress the diagnostic first and investigate only if a user reports a production failure.
Treat untrusted JSON or command-line input as statically validated simply because the program uses Dart.
Add an unrelated package or a broad refactor before reproducing the reported behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reduce the failure to a small case, inspect the complete diagnostic and inputs, verify the documented SDK/target constraints, and test one change at a time.
questions.explanation: Reducing a failure and inspecting full diagnostics avoids speculative changes and exposes SDK/platform assumptions.
